text: The spirometry confirms an obstructive pattern consistent with COPD. Have you noticed any swelling in your ankles or a change in the color of your skin, such as a bluish tint? REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas Also, do you experience chest pain or palpitations when you exert yourself?

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood gas results are normal, which is good news for your oxygenation. Given your history of heavy smoking and construction work, along with the confirmed obstructive pattern, do you experience any sudden episodes of severe shortness of breath or wheezing that come and go?

text: No, I don't have those sudden episodes of severe shortness of breath or wheezing that come and go. My breathing just feels generally tight and labored, especially when I try to climb stairs or walk a bit further than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: That steady, progressive dyspnea without acute reversibility further supports a diagnosis of chronic COPD rather than asthma.
